blocks.title: When trimming **will not fix it.**
body: Some shrubs are past saving with shears. The yews are up to the windows, the junipers have gone bare inside, and the bushes planted when the house was new now hide it. At that point the honest fix is to take them out and start the bed over.
We dig them out roots and all. On bigger jobs a compact track loader does the heavy pulling while the crew works the edges by hand, and everything goes out in our dump trailer.

blocks.title: Cut it at the ground and **it comes back.**
blocks.intro: Plenty of shrubs sprout again from what is left underground. Michigan State University Extension is blunt about two common ones.

items.title: Bush honeysuckle
items.body: Amur, Tatarian and Morrow's honeysuckle leaf out early and stay green late. MSU says any roots left in the ground re-sprout easily, and stems that are only clipped sprout back hard.

items.title: Buckthorn
items.body: Cut buckthorn stumps sprout back vigorously, MSU says. Its fruit turns from red to black in clusters, and some people mistake it for a cherry.

items.title: New state rules
items.body: From January 1, 2028, Michigan restricts common buckthorn, glossy buckthorn and Japanese barberry, named varieties included. MSU says homeowners who already have them are not in violation and do not have to act right away.

blocks.title: Look, mark, **dig, haul.**

steps.title: Rob looks first
steps.body: Rob walks the beds with you, points out what can stay and what should go, and quotes the job. The estimate is free.

steps.title: Lines get marked
steps.body: MISS DIG 811 needs a ticket at least 3 business days before any digging, and whoever digs places it. Private lines are not marked, so tell us about sprinkler lines, dog fences or power to a shed.

steps.title: Out they come
steps.body: Bushes and small trees come out with their root balls, by hand or with a compact track loader, depending on their size and how easy they are to reach.

steps.title: Hauled away
steps.body: Branches, roots and clumps of soil go into our dump trailer and leave with us. The bed is open and ready to [rebuild](/landscaping/) or [mulch](/mulch-and-flower-beds/).

blocks.footnote: Removal is often the first day of a bed rebuild. Bob S. had his 25 year old bushes and a cherry tree taken out, the bed rescaped, fabric and mulch laid and a natural edge cut, and wrote that it was all done in two days.

blocks.intro: A rough guide. Rob will give you his honest read when he sees the shrub, and sometimes [a good trim](/shrub-trimming/) is all it needs.

blocks.title: Big trees are **not ours.**
body: We take out bushes, shrubs and small trees, the kind we can pull with the roots, like the cherry tree in Bob S.'s review. Big trees, and the stumps they leave, are not our work.

For a big tree, call a tree company first. MSU Extension advises leaving tall trees and large branches to people with the skills and equipment for them, and anything near power lines to the utility. Once the tree is gone, we can rebuild the bed around where it stood.

blocks.title: Old bushes and a cherry tree, **out.**

faq.q: Do you remove bushes in Grand Blanc?
faq.a: Yes. Grand Scapes digs out overgrown bushes, shrubs and small trees, roots and all, across Grand Blanc and Grand Blanc Township, and hauls them away. We do removals across Genesee County and north Oakland County too.
Small trees, yes, like the cherry tree in one of our Google reviews. Big trees are not our work. For those, call a tree company, and we can rebuild the bed once the tree is gone.

faq.q: Do you get the roots out?
faq.a: Yes. We pull the root ball, not just the top, because many shrubs sprout back from roots left in the ground. MSU Extension says bush honeysuckle re-sprouts easily from leftover roots, and cut buckthorn stumps sprout back vigorously.

faq.q: Do you haul away the bushes?
faq.a: Yes. Branches, roots and debris go into our dump trailer and leave with us. You are left with an open bed, ready to replant or mulch.

faq.q: Should I remove or trim my overgrown shrubs?
faq.a: If the shrub still fits its spot and is green inside, a trim may bring it back. If it has outgrown the window, is bare inside or is mostly dead, removal is usually the better call. Junipers in particular do not regrow from bare inner branches, MSU Extension notes. Rob will give you his honest read.

faq.q: Do I need to call MISS DIG to remove bushes?
faq.a: Yes, someone does. MISS DIG 811 says any digging project needs a ticket at least 3 business days ahead, regardless of size or depth, and the person or company doing the digging places it. MISS DIG does not mark private lines like sprinkler lines, invisible dog fences or power to a shed, so point those out to us.

faq.q: Can I get rid of my Japanese barberry or buckthorn?
faq.a: Yes. Starting January 1, 2028, Michigan restricts Japanese barberry, common buckthorn and glossy buckthorn, so they can no longer be sold. MSU Extension says homeowners who already have them are not in violation and do not have to act right away. If you want them out, we dig them out roots and all, since buckthorn sprouts back hard from a stump.

faq.q: How much does bush removal cost?
faq.a: It depends on how many shrubs there are, how big they are, how deep the roots go and how easy it is to get a machine to them. Rob looks at it and quotes a price, and the estimate is free.
